holidays.name: National Talk in an Elevator Day
holidays.description: Today is your excuse to break the great elevator silence. Skip the awkward stare at the floor numbers and say something to the people riding with you. A compliment, a weather remark, or a bold hot take on the lobby music will all do.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It plays on the shared social awkwardness of riding in tiny metal boxes with strangers.
holidays.funFact: Elevator safety took a big leap in 1854. Elisha Otis dramatically demonstrated his safety brake at the New York Crystal Palace exhibition by having the hoisting rope cut while he stood on the platform.

holidays.name: National All or Nothing Day
holidays.description: This is a day for commitment. Whether it's finally starting the project, eating the whole pizza, or skipping the half-measures, today is about going big. Pick your thing and give it everything.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It's a motivational occasion that encourages people to stop dabbling and fully commit.
holidays.funFact: The all-or-nothing idea has old roots. The Latin motto "Aut Caesar aut nihil", meaning "Either Caesar or nothing", is attributed to the Renaissance figure Cesare Borgia.

holidays.name: National Aunt and Uncle Day
holidays.description: This day celebrates the fun relatives who spoil us, share family secrets, and slip us snacks before dinner. Call, visit, or send a thank-you to the aunts and uncles (and honorary ones) who made your childhood better.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It's a family-focused occasion that gives aunts and uncles a day of their own.
holidays.funFact: There's a dedicated word for uncle-like behavior: "avuncular" describes someone who is kindly, genial, and protective in the manner of a favorite uncle.
